# Jubilees Chapter 37 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Esau attacks Jacob; the battle in the hills of Hebron

---

**37:1** In the first year of the first week of the forty-sixth jubilee, Esau returned against his brother Jacob to make war against him.

**37:2** He had heard that Jacob had accumulated great wealth at Hebron — silver, gold, cattle, camels, and horses. Esau gathered four thousand warriors and came against Jacob into the land of Canaan.

**37:3** When Jacob heard that Esau was coming against him with four thousand men, he was afraid. He built a fortified tower and constructed a stone wall around it.

**37:4** Jacob sent word to his brother Esau: "I have seen your face as one sees the face of God, and you have been gracious to me. Why do you come against me with swords and shields to kill me and my household?"

**37:5** Esau replied: "Even though I swore peace with you before your mother Rebekah, I have not forgotten the days when you deceived me and the wrong you did to me."

**37:6** Jacob said to his sons and his household: "Arm yourselves and come out against Esau, for he is coming against us with a great force."

**37:7** Jacob's sons armed themselves — Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, and Joseph — and four hundred men with them.

**37:8** They went out against Esau and his four thousand men. A great battle was fought in the hill country of Hebron.

**37:9** Judah killed Adoran, Dan killed his opponent, Naphtali killed his adversary, and Gad killed his.

**37:10** Reuben killed the king of the Arameans who had come with Esau. The battle raged fiercely all that day.

**37:11** At the end of the day, Esau fled with his men and returned to Seir. Jacob and his sons pursued them to the border of Seir.

**37:12** Esau made peace again with Jacob and they swore a second oath, saying: "Let there be peace between us from this day until the end of our lives."

**37:13** Jacob's sons turned back from the pursuit and returned to Hebron.

**37:14** Jacob and his sons rested after the battle and rejoiced greatly, for Esau had been driven back.

**37:15** On that day, Isaac died at the age of one hundred and eighty years, in the forty-sixth jubilee, fifth week, first year.

**37:16** Jacob buried his father at Mamre in the cave of Machpelah, alongside his grandparents Abraham and Sarah.

---

*LOGOS notes: The Jacob-Esau war tradition is found also in the Testament of Judah 9 and likely comes from a common Aramaic source. In Jubilees' logic, Esau's attack is the fulfillment of the Mastema warning and vindicates Jacob's righteousness. The battle details are specific and somewhat stylized.*
